construct.name: procedural participation, proposal traceability and facilitator steering
construct.intended_use: Verify that speaking inequality, proposal omission, evidence support, consensus endorsements and allocation perturbations are measured as separate trace properties.
construct.claim_ceiling: Tier 1 synthetic procedural-audit reference only; no human-subject effect, causal facilitation estimate or legitimate-welfare claim.

units.dependence_statement: Members, turns, proposals and allocations are nested within the same synthetic sessions; no independent sample or human population is represented.

sources.missingness_semantics: The deterministic fixture has complete declared cells; absent cells are missing/unsupported, never zero.

evaluation_distribution.sampling_frame: Two synthetic three-member sessions with recorded preferences, turns, proposals, evidence references, endorsement flags and a fixed 100-unit allocation budget; plus paired rhetoric and option-order controls.

factors.weight_interpretation: Two authored software fixtures; equal design coverage, not prevalence.
Paired semantic-order tests, not population-weighted observations.

perturbation_families.rationale: Tests whether a changed facilitation trace moves allocation while participant preferences and evidence remain fixed.
perturbation_families.validity_check: Compare semantic input identity, preference vectors and evidence catalogue before interpreting allocation shift.
expected_invariants: Participant preference vectors are identical across paired sessions.
Evidence catalogue and source digests are identical across paired sessions.
perturbation_families.seed_policy: Deterministic authored fixture; no stochastic seed.

perturbation_families.rationale: Tests whether position labels or order change allocation after remapping back to semantic option IDs.
perturbation_families.validity_check: Compare options by stable semantic labels, not array position.
expected_invariants: A pure display permutation with equivalent semantic allocation yields zero shift.
Deliberate position bias yields a non-zero semantic allocation shift.
perturbation_families.seed_policy: Deterministic authored permutation; no stochastic seed.

replication_design.independent_unit: One fixed deterministic design matrix; no stochastic or empirical replication is claimed.
replication_design.dependence_assessment: Scenario, strategy, participant and condition cells are deterministic benchmark fixtures, not independent draws from a target population.
replication_design.sample_size_rationale: One deterministic execution is sufficient to verify exact code paths and negative controls; it cannot support confidence intervals or population inference.

metrics.aggregation: Gini over participant speaking-time totals within each session
unique proposals raised in turns that are represented in the summary divided by unique proposals raised
claims lacking a known evidence ID with a source-declared verified status

metrics.construct_dimension: declared consensus rule versus recorded endorsements
metrics.aggregation: true only when a facilitator consensus declaration conflicts with an assessed explicit consensus rule; missing endorsement remains unknown
L1 over semantic options; reallocated units are L1/2

baselines.description: Recorded baseline session with fixed declared preferences and equal semantic allocation.
Deterministic preference-proportional counterfactual; descriptive only, not a welfare optimum.

negative_controls.intervention: Replace a participant consensus endorsement with null.
negative_controls.expected_result: Consensus rule status becomes unknown when available endorsements cannot establish the declared threshold; missing is not counted as dissent.

negative_controls.intervention: Permute option order and remap preferences, proposal meanings and final allocation by stable option labels.
negative_controls.expected_result: Pure semantic invariance produces zero allocation shift; the position-biased fixture produces 56 L1 units.

negative_controls.intervention: Add a facilitator claim referencing an unknown evidence ID.
negative_controls.expected_result: The claim is counted unsupported and cannot be represented as evidence-backed.

holdouts.leakage_control: No empirical rows are used; this reference supports no external-generalization claim.

reproduction.runtime_environment: Rust edition 2024; deterministic benchmark crate; exact-head GitHub Actions workflow
reproduction.humanity_atlas_run_artifact_ref: Not applicable: synthetic benchmark reference execution; no full Humanity Atlas scenario artifact is claimed.

claim_report.claim_ceiling: Tier 1 synthetic procedural-audit reference only; no human-subject effect, causal facilitation estimate or legitimate-welfare claim.
known_limitations: Turn durations and proposal references are hand-authored event traces.
Evidence verification is only a source-declared boolean in this reference; the kernel does not independently authenticate source bytes.
Preference-proportional allocation is a descriptive counterfactual, not a normative welfare optimum.
Satisfaction and trust are self-reported synthetic values.
unsupported_strata: Human deliberation groups, languages, cultures, institutional settings, real facilitators and high-stakes public decisions.

components.notes: Synthetic oracle or explicit deterministic controller; not a human or LLM.
Stable serial execution in declared input order.
Reject invalid or out-of-contract inputs; no silent repair.
Capture every declared input, step, output and metric; missing records fail closed.
No unseeded random source is used by this deterministic fixture.

scheduler_policy.update_order: stable declared fixture order; deterministic serial execution
scheduler_policy.tie_breaking_rule: stable identifier then stable input index

exposure_policy.eligibility_rule: not applicable to this deterministic reference fixture
exposure_policy.state_visibility: all declared synthetic inputs are visible to the benchmark runner
